claims.statement: Charter completeness is decided by a raw `ygg.kv.get("task.<piece>")` plus `trim` on title/goal/success — never through the defaulting `config.task_*` accessors, because a fallback value would make an empty charter look complete.
`run.begin` refuses with `charter_missing` when any of the three pieces is empty: the completeness gate lives at the act itself, not only downstream at `coordinate.submit`.

`charter.set` is accepted only while `run_phase()` is the charter phase; anywhere else it rejects with `charter_locked` and names the current phase, and `run.begin` likewise refuses outside that phase.

`run.begin` calls `readsig.clear()` before narrating `[RUN BEGUN]`: signatures taken for the charter act do not carry into the coordinate act, so a signature is a per-act ticket rather than a one-time pass.

Zero requirements is caught later, at `coordinate.submit`, by the `gate_charter_first` gate — the two gates sit at different points on purpose, so a run can be chartered and still be told it has nothing to dispatch.
The payload is `<title>|<goal>|<success>` parsed by `wire.parse_charter`, and a malformed payload returns a problem text instead of a partially written charter.
`charter.set` and `run.begin` are exempt from the human-approval ticket gate (R5): they are the run owner's own declaration and a start-of-work statement, not a human milestone action.

The act menu keeps one next-step question that names only the action — revise the charter, then begin once the three pieces are complete — because the meaning of the three pieces is this page's job, not the prompt's.
